name: p2-wbdmac-f6-ram-len8
notes: one Ibex RVFI OBI CPU, the PULP timer as the F5 source, and the pinned configs/peripherals/zipcpu_wbdmac profile, whose RTL is third_party/soc-zipcpu/rtl/peripherals/wbdmac.v: a pipelined Wishbone memory master plus a registered-ack control target, i.e. a different device from the ZipDMA (rtl/zipdma/*), not a second profile of it

the F6 firmware writes the plan start word 0x0fed0004 (key 0xfed in bits 27:16, block length in bits 9:0) to the control word, waits for the transfer, then reads the control status back; the destination block is read back by the CPU
the transfer is RAM -> RAM: the DMA master really reads the source block it was configured with and really writes the destination block, and the case line reports both beat counts

eight words: the deepest block this entry executes (DMA_MAX_BLOCK_WORDS = 8, MAILBOX_BYTES = INPUT_BLOCK + 4*8).  The pinned block-length field is LGMEMLEN = 10 bits, so eight words is a real part of the device range and not a host maximum dressed up as one
